content:
Phase 35 plan submitted: docs/phases/cross-project-hub-30-arc.md (brief: docs/tagteam-3.0-proposal.md §4 Phase 35, §8 Q7). Branch phase-35-cross-project-hub; PR at the end; release 0.12.0.

Designed flow-first with the ux-design-guide skill (the plan's "UX design" section): user goal "across all my projects — what needs me, is anything stuck, how much am I burning"; principles IA by intent, visual hierarchy / Von Restorff, progressive disclosure (≤2 clicks), Tesler / smart defaults. Grounded in the REAL registry on this machine: 43 dirs, 21 with a handoff state, a long quiet tail, two turns owed for days/weeks unnoticed, scratch dirs registered as noise.

Scope: (1) `tagteam hub [--port 8090] [--host 127.0.0.1] [--interval] [--max-sse] [--all]` server + `tagteam hub --list [--json]` text mode; flag-off identical (no other command changes; registry format unchanged; no new files unless `tagteam hub` runs). (2) `hub_api.py` pure: registry classification (needs_you / waiting / quiet / hidden), ranking + staleness rules (stale = owed ≥30 min with no in-flight and no watcher; abandoned ≥24 h), per-project error isolation, aggregate usage over 24h/7d/all, shared subscription window = newest rate_limits row across projects; **read-only DB access** (`file:…?mode=ro`, never `_migrate` — a v3 project stays v3; test), §8 Q7 answered with a writer-holds-transaction test. (3) Hub server on `TagteamHTTPServer`: `/`, `/api/hub`, `/api/hub/usage`, SSE `/api/hub/events` (file-signal signature over all projects, no DB per tick), and **cockpits mounted at `/p/<id>/`** (the Phase 34 handler per project, one per-run token, loopback default, same Origin check) so acting is two clicks from the hub — no per-project servers. (4) Cockpit base-path: one mode-agnostic `<meta name="tagteam-base">` in cockpit.js/html (absent → identical requests today; regression test) + "← Hub" link only when mounted. (5) `hub.html|css|js`: top strip (N projects · M live, burn, shared window, Live/Polling), Needs you (single primary action Open), Waiting (badges + stale/abandoned with CLI hints), Quiet collapsed to a count, hidden toggle, empty states. (6) Registry hygiene: `tagteam registry list|unregister` (thin glue), scratch/no-yaml dirs hidden by default. (7) Docs/findings/dogfood over the real registry (stale rows surface with correct ages; ruling on a scratch escalation via the mounted cockpit; SSE across projects).

Open questions with recommendations: mount cockpits under the hub vs link out (recommend mount); default port 8090; staleness thresholds 30 min / 24 h as shipped defaults; hide /tmp-style and no-tagteam.yaml dirs by default with `--all`. Please review against docs/checklists/plan_review.md.

The hub direction and UX hierarchy are strong, but the plan needs the following contract-level revisions before implementation:

1. Replace the proposed “cached handler instances + path rewriting” mount design with a viable request-dispatch architecture. `server.make_handler()` returns a `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` subclass whose instances are constructed per socket/request and immediately enter request handling; those instances cannot safely be cached or delegated to from `HubHandler`. Specify the reusable seam (for example, factor cockpit GET/POST dispatch into a shared router/mixin invoked by standalone and hub handlers) and cache only immutable per-project context / SSE state, never handler instances. Define isolation and tests for two projects concurrently so reads, writes, SSE slots, path state, and auth cannot bleed between mounts.

Also make the base-path/static contract internally consistent: JS can prefix API/EventSource/navigation URLs from the meta tag, but it cannot retroactively prefix the HTML’s `<link href="/cockpit.css">` and `<script src="/cockpit.js">`. Choose and document either root-shared static assets or server-injected/base-aware HTML URLs, and test the exact mounted URLs plus byte-identical standalone routing.

2. Define non-mutating registry reads. `get_registered_projects()` currently removes missing directories and rewrites `~/.tagteam/projects.json`, so it cannot support the stated “missing dir -> hidden, revealed by --all” behavior and makes `hub --list` mutate the registry. Add/use an explicit raw read path for hub/list, state whether `registry list` shows raw or existing entries, and test that all read/list modes leave the registry byte-for-byte unchanged while `unregister` is the only requested mutation.

3. Make the cross-project read-only boundary and live invalidation exhaustive. `cockpit_api.now_payload()` calls `db.connect()` and migrates, so “reuses now_payload pieces” must name safe factored helpers or direct readers and prohibit invoking any migrating aggregate. Test that an absent DB remains absent as well as v3-v5 `user_version` preservation. The SSE signature must cover every value displayed by `/api/hub`: the current enumerated file signals omit DB/WAL changes (usage and rate limits) and process-scan-only watcher liveness, so a connected client can remain Live while totals or watcher state are stale. Include cheap DB/WAL mtimes and actual liveness (or a specified periodic snapshot refresh), with tests for a DB-only update and a watcher start/exit that has no pidfile.

4. Correct the shared-window and abandonment semantics. `rate_limits` intentionally stores one current row per `(provider, kind)` (for example five-hour and seven-day); selecting one newest row across all projects can discard another active window. Aggregate the newest row per `(provider, kind)` across projects, document the payload shape/tie-break, and test competing timestamps for multiple kinds. Likewise, make `abandoned` a refinement of stale (`owed >= 24h` and no inflight/watcher), not merely age-based, so a demonstrably live long-running turn is not labeled abandoned; add the boundary/liveness case.

Once those contracts and success criteria are explicit, the recommended defaults (mounting, 8090, 30m/24h, hidden scratch/no-yaml entries) are reasonable.

Round 2: all four contract points folded into docs/phases/cross-project-hub-30-arc.md (Scope 2/3/3b/4/6, Files, ranking rules, success criteria; Open Questions → Decisions).

1. Dispatch architecture: handler instances are per-request and never cached/delegated. The cockpit routing is factored out of `make_handler` into a `CockpitRouter` in server.py — immutable per-project context only (project_dir, token, max_sse, base_path, its own SSE lock + count) with `handle_get(h, parsed, path)` / `handle_post(h, path)` / `check_write_auth(h)` / `sse(h)` taking the live handler; `make_handler` builds one router and delegates (standalone unchanged, existing tests unmodified); the hub's `HubHandler` caches `{project_id: CockpitRouter}` (context, not handlers), strips `/p/<id>/` and delegates. Isolation by construction (own project_dir, own SSE counter/cap, never sees another mount's path) plus tests with two projects mounted concurrently: pause via /p/a affects A only; ruling via /p/a/api/rule records in A only; per-mount SSE frames and caps; missing/wrong token 403 on either; unknown id 404. Base-path/static made consistent: server-injected base-aware HTML — `_get_dashboard_html(theme, token, base_path)` rewrites the page's root-relative asset URLs to `<base>/…` and injects `<meta name="tagteam-base">`; JS prefixes fetch/EventSource/navigation from the meta; assets served under the mount by the router's static branch; exact mounted URLs tested; standalone `base_path=""` → no rewrite/no meta, served page and requests identical to 0.11.0 (test).

2. Registry: `get_registered_projects()` prunes+rewrites on read, so the hub gets a new public `read_registry_raw()` (+ `registry_path()`), no pruning, no write; `hub`, `hub --list`, `/api/hub` and `tagteam registry list` use it; `registry list` shows raw entries with markers (missing / no tagteam.yaml / scratch / ok); missing dirs are hidden and revealable with `--all`; `unregister` is the only mutation. Tests: every read/list mode leaves projects.json byte-for-byte unchanged (incl. with a missing dir present); `get_registered_projects()` untouched for upgrade/rollback.

3. Read-only boundary made exhaustive: `hub_api.py` builds summaries ONLY from non-migrating readers (read_state, read_status, read_pause/read_inflight, read_pidfile, procs via the DB-free `cockpit_api.watcher_status`, and `read_only_connect(dir)` = `file:…?mode=ro` or None when absent — never creates .tagteam/, never migrates); it never calls `now_payload()` or `db.connect()` — enforced by a grep test. Tests: absent DB stays absent, v3/v4/v5 user_version preserved, corrupt DB → row with error, writer holding `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` while the hub reads. SSE signature covers every displayed value: per project state/rounds file mtime+size, pause marker, inflight stem/pid AND pid-alive, watcher pidfile pid-alive AND process-scan liveness from ONE shared `procs.list_processes` snapshot per tick, DB and -wal mtimes+sizes (usage/rate_limits/briefs/interjections without opening the DB), plus registry mtime; 30 s periodic snapshot refresh in live mode as belt-and-braces. Tests: DB-only usage write → frame; watcher process start/exit without a pidfile → frames both ways; registry edit → frame.

4. Shared window: newest row per `(provider, kind)` across projects (tie-break later ts, then registry order), payload `rate_limits: [{provider, kind, status, resets_at, ts, project}]`, all kinds in the strip; test with competing timestamps for five_hour vs seven_day across two projects. `abandoned` = stale ∧ owed ≥ 24 h (a refinement of stale; a live long-running turn or running watcher is never abandoned); boundary (29m59s vs 30m) and live-25h cases tested.

Defaults confirmed as recommended (mount, 8090, 30 min / 24 h, hidden scratch/no-yaml/missing with --all). No arbiter interjections were pending.

Approved. Round 2 resolves the requested architecture, registry, read-only/live-refresh, rate-limit aggregation, and abandonment contracts with specific isolation and regression tests. The plan is feasible and ready for implementation.
